title: Book 9 — Calliope, Chapter 38
paragraphs: The death of Hegesistratos, however, occurred later than the events at Plataea; at this time he was at the Asopos, having been hired by Mardonius for no small sum, sacrificing and showing zeal for his cause both because of his enmity toward the Lacedaemonians and because of the money he was earning. But as the sacrifices were not favorable for battle either for the Persians themselves or for those Greeks with them (they too had their own diviner, Hippomachos the Leucadian), and as the Greeks had men constantly streaming in and growing in number, Timagenides son of Herpys, a Theban, counseled Mardonius to set a guard on the pass of Kithairon, saying that the Greeks were pouring in every day and he would thus cut off large numbers.
